assertions: He will not obtain the desired parsonage (benefice)

There is no perfection of the matter: Jupiter, lord of the 9th and significator of the benefice, makes no aspect to the lord of the Ascendant or to the Moon, and there is no reception, translation or collection of light between the significators
Saturn impedited in the Ascendant infortunes the question and the querent: the suit is obstructed and labour, time and solicitation are spent in vain
Neither the lord of the Ascendant nor the Moon is placed in the 9th, showing no connection of the querent to the benefice

The Moon separating from a trine and applying to an opposition of Mercury, lord of the 3rd, brings opposition, adverse report or contention by way of messages, kindred or neighbours, ending in disappointment and regret
Venus in the 7th in opposition to the Ascendant shows an opposing party / rival side set against him, so the benefice is withheld from him rather than granted
summary: He will not obtain the parsonage he desires; the suit fails despite his pressing it.
method: Lilly horary astrology (Christian Astrology, Book II), 9th-house benefice question, classical significators and perfection testimonies
reasoning: Querent = lord of Ascendant + Moon; quesited benefice = Jupiter lord of 9th. Lilly's seven negative testimonies all deny perfection: Saturn impedited in Ascendant afflicts the question, no aspect/reception/translation/collection between querent and Jupiter, neither querent significator in 9th, Moon applying to opposition of Mercury lord of 3rd, and Venus in 7th opposing Ascendant. With no joining of significators, horary rule is the matter will not be perfected.
